clue.text: They make dough for bread — or vice versa

definitions.text: They make dough for bread — or vice versa

parts.words: They make dough for bread — or vice versa
parts.note: dough and bread are both slang for money, so a place turning dough into loaves is also one turning bread into cash

explanation.surface: A riddle about businesses that turn money into more money.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, bakers' premises mix dough to make bread; read as slang, dough and bread both mean money, so they earn their 'bread' from dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops and premises where loaves are baked from kneaded flour mixture are exactly what the clue describes.

parts.note: asking a higher court to review a verdict is a request for a superior body's ruling

explanation.definitionFit: Taking a case to a higher court for a fresh ruling is the legal sense of the word.

clue.text: Be first to be introduced by former partner

indicators.note: the second piece is brought in after, led on by the former partner, so that comes first

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
1st, written with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be the first to meet an ex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is abbreviated 1ST, and the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being or reality.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of these words might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is either a fool or rather entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OR AMUSING into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant, foolish person, a dunce.

clue.text: Like hell cats in a melee

indicators.note: a melee is a confused scrum, so the letters of these words are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Cats fighting in a scrum make a hellish din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a melee' looks like a phrase, but 'in a' is fodder: 'melee' scrambles CATSINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, belonging to Satan and so to hell.

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means majestic and venerable
the eighth month of the calendar

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means venerable and grand; the noun is the summer month.

indicators.note: the middle of the word means all its letters but the first and last

explanation.surface: A plant that grows in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle Eastern' reads as a region, but it means the middle of the word Eastern.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like flowering garden plant.

clue.text: Whip up strikes in sporting associations

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: to flog is to whip
to club is to strike with a cudgel

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up industrial action within sports clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip up' looks like 'arouse'; 'up' turns FLOG to GOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs are societies of golfers, a kind of sporting association.

clue.text: Wade about in a Scottish river for sport

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the river

parts.note: the Spey is a river in Scotland, famous for salmon and whisky

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: An angler wades into a Scottish river for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wade' looks like the angler's action, but 'about' scrambles it and 'in' places the result within the river; 'sport' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedway is motorcycle racing on dirt tracks, a spectator sport.

clue.text: Love to point out there's a choice

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A loving person points out that there is a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' is an anagram signal working on 'point' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is an alternative one may pick, a choice.

clue.text: Summed up as tale told inaccurately

indicators.note: told inaccurately means the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An account is summarised by a tale told badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To total figures is to add them up, sum them.

parts.note: a cast is the set of actors in a production
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Strong performers join a club together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron means rigid and robust, figuratively unbreakable.

clue.text: About to give way and go back

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to cede is to yield or give way

explanation.surface: Someone is about to yield and retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or withdraw.

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house and a circular is a leaflet, so a flyer advertising one

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a half-round form; split, it is a leaflet for a half of a pair of houses.

definitions.meaning: a trace or hint, as in a touch of garlic
a feeling that something is wrong, mistrust

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both a slight trace of something and a sense of mistrust.

definitions.meaning: to dash from one side to the other

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a dash to the other side; idiomatically, to come upon someone by chance.

parts.note: the public are people in general

explanation.surface: Customers want a new landlord for their local.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican runs a pub, and is called its landlord in Britain.

parts.note: the cords that close a money bag are what one holds when in charge of spending

explanation.definitionFit: Whoever holds the cords of the money bag controls spending, as in the idiom about holding them.

clue.text: Right to get overjoyed when told

parts.note: elated means overjoyed

explanation.surface: Someone is entitled to be thrilled at the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Related is a synonym of recounted or narrated, as when a story is told.

clue.text: Flat for those not wishing to move when they retire

definitions.text: Flat for those not wishing to move when they retire

parts.words: Flat for those not wishing to move when they retire
parts.note: retire here means go to bed, and someone too lazy to move would sit on the bed in a one-room flat

explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' suggests pensioners; it means going to bed. A bedsit is a British one-room rented flat where bed and sitting room are one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single-room flat combining bedroom and sitting room.

clue.text: Fighting together, every single one die in action

parts.note: all means every single one

indicators.note: in action suggests the letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Allies fighting side by side, all prepared to die in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means joined in alliance, as forces fighting on the same side.

definitions.meaning: to ready food, as in readying a salad or a chicken
the military order for soldiers to align their ranks

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is readying food or a wound; the other is the drill command to align ranks.

clue.text: One permitted to break silence up to a point

indicators.note: to break the word is to smash its letters into a new order

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone allowed to break a silence, though only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges SILENCE to LICENSE; 'up to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee holds a licence, so is someone officially permitted, typically to sell alcohol.

indicators.note: to force something is to wrench it out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A pilot is made to bring the aircraft down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' rearranges PLANE; 'land' looks like a verb but is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country, a land.

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A kitchen disaster: someone is unable to chop bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the thing being diced, but it is the anagram signal for CANTDICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is a mishap or misfortune, a calamity.

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a pose is an attitude or posture

explanation.surface: A stance at work used for resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose is to resist or set oneself against.

clue.text: Fruit with the head off will still be fruit

indicators.note: the head is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: bananas are a fruit

explanation.surface: Lopping the top off a fruit leaves you with fruit still.
explanation.walkthrough: Ananas is another name for the pineapple, used in many languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the pineapple, a tropical fruit.

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: late means dead, deceased

explanation.surface: Female deer laid out dead make a sad sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' is female deer, not the verb; 'set out' rearranges it to DESO.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means wretched, forlorn, utterly miserable.
